notes: Scenario repositories are built by make-eval-scenarios.sh into <workspace>/scenarios. Each prompt runs with the scenario repository as the working directory and points the skill at the fake upstream with --repo-url, so the evals need no network and do not depend on the published template.

evals.name: diverged-with-conflict
evals.prompt: Run claude-md-downstream in repo mode for this repository. We mirror the ai-store repo internally, so use <UPSTREAM> as the upstream instead of the public GitHub one.
evals.expected_output: Reports the file as diverged, names the closest template version with its commit and link, separates the upstream changes from the project's own, raises the commit-rule conflict on its own and waits, keeps the Build and Test and Deployment sections untouched, and writes nothing without approval.
assertions: Reports the file as diverged and names the closest template version by commit SHA
Presents the commit-rule conflict on its own, showing both the upstream and the local wording
Names the upstream commit (subject or SHA) that caused the conflict
The project's 'Build and Test' section survives verbatim in the final CLAUDE.md
The project's 'Deployment' section survives verbatim in the final CLAUDE.md
The local 'Never commit on main' instruction is still present in the final CLAUDE.md
The upstream verification rule was applied to the final CLAUDE.md
The upstream 'Stage files by name' clause was applied to the final CLAUDE.md
The upstream 'unless another specific language is expressly requested' clause was applied
A timestamped backup of the previous CLAUDE.md exists next to it
No git commit was created in the scenario repository
Asked for approval before writing, and the question is recorded verbatim

evals.name: known-older-version
evals.prompt: I think our CLAUDE.md is out of date. Use the claude-md-downstream skill, repo mode, against our internal mirror at <UPSTREAM>.
evals.expected_output: Reports that the file matches an older template verbatim, names that commit with SHA, date and subject, and says once that this mirror has no browsable commit view instead of inventing a link, lists what has landed since, says that nothing local would be lost, asks whether to take the current version, and writes nothing without approval.
assertions: Reports that the file matches an older template verbatim
Names the matched commit with SHA, date and subject
Reports the matched commit by SHA and does not fabricate a link for the mirror upstream
Lists the template changes that have landed since the matched commit
States that nothing local would be lost by taking the current version
Asks whether to take the current version instead of writing unprompted
After approval the final CLAUDE.md equals the current upstream template
A timestamped backup of the previous CLAUDE.md exists next to it
No git commit was created in the scenario repository

evals.name: identical-restraint
evals.prompt: run claude-md-downstream repo mode, upstream is <UPSTREAM>
evals.expected_output: Reports in a few lines that CLAUDE.md is current, naming the upstream commit. Offers nothing, asks nothing, changes nothing.
assertions: Reports that CLAUDE.md is current
Names the upstream commit it matches
CLAUDE.md is byte-identical to before the run
No backup file was created
Asked the user nothing
The report is brief — no offers, no proposals, no follow-up work

evals.name: take-template-1-1
evals.prompt: Run claude-md-downstream in repo mode against our internal mirror at <UPSTREAM>. The local edits in that file are leftovers from an experiment nobody stands behind any more — if it has drifted from the template, I just want the template as it is now, not a merge.
evals.expected_output: Reports the file as diverged, recognises that the user is asking for the whole-file route rather than a per-conflict merge, lists in full what taking the template 1:1 would remove (both local sections with their rules, the local commit-rule clause, the bent simplicity rule), says the removed text survives in the backup, asks once for confirmation, and only then writes the current template verbatim with a timestamped backup and no commit.
assertions: Reports the file as diverged before offering anything
Takes the whole-file route instead of walking the user through the conflicts one by one
Lists what the 1:1 take removes, quoting the local rules rather than only counting them
Names both local sections ('Build and Test', 'Deployment') among the losses
Names the local 'Never commit on main' clause among the losses
States that the removed text survives in the timestamped backup
Asks once for confirmation before writing, rather than treating the prompt as approval
The final CLAUDE.md equals the current upstream template verbatim
No local-only rule survives in the final CLAUDE.md
A timestamped backup of the previous CLAUDE.md exists next to it
No git commit was created in the scenario repository
